proposed_statement_changes.proposed:
Restrict attention to legal triangular arrays for which
\[
\liminf_{N\to\infty}\frac{K_N}{N^{q_d}}=0,
\]
equivalently, arrays that are not eventually bounded below by any positive constant multiple of \(N^{q_d}\). Using \(\mathfrak H_{\mathrm{frontier}}\), determine explicit rate functions \(\rho_{\mathrm{est}}(N,K)\) and \(\rho_{\mathrm{len}}(N,K)\) such that
\[
R_d(N,K)\asymp\rho_{\mathrm{est}}(N,K),
\qquad
E_{d,\alpha}(N,K)\asymp\rho_{\mathrm{len}}(N,K)
\]
along every such array, including the exact fixed-\(K\) logarithms and every transition. The answer must be subsequence-stable: for every subsequence \(\mathcal S\) on which \(K_N/N^{q_d}\) remains arbitrarily small, meaning
\[
\liminf_{N\to\infty,\,N\in\mathcal S}\frac{K_N}{N^{q_d}}=0,
\]
it must establish the asserted rates on every further subsequence \(\mathcal T\subseteq\mathcal S\) for which \(K_N/N^{q_d}\to0\), and it must combine those rates with the established root-\(N\) bounds on further subsequences where \(K_N/N^{q_d}\) is bounded below by a positive constant. Thus an array that oscillates between small- and large-arm regimes may not be discarded. The lower-bound branch must instantiate the finite-support simultaneous family so that \(\Delta_{N,K}\) matches the claimed rate, \(\operatorname{TV}_{\mathrm{mix}}\le1/4\), and \(\mathfrak g_{\mathrm{rem}}>0\), thereby giving nonnegative reduced cost against every rematching column and strict slack off the declared contact columns; its ordered low-versus-high version must also prove the one-sided expected-excess-length converse. The upper-bound branch must construct a computable estimator and a uniformly honest lower confidence bound with numerically specified calibration attaining the respective rates, or prove a sharper shared-geometric dual bound and supply the calibration needed for honesty. The existence of the unspecified constant \(C_d\) in \(B_N^{\mathrm{plug}}\) alone does not make that theoretical rule numerically computable.
proposed_statement_changes.reason: The current question still quantifies over every legal array even though the root-\(N\) region has been settled. The honest residual class is the complement of eventual positive-multiple growth, namely \(\liminf_N K_N/N^{q_d}=0\). Stating subsequence stability is necessary because an irregular array can alternate between proved large-arm indices and unresolved arbitrarily small ratios; restricting only to arrays with a full-sequence limit \(K_N/N^{q_d}\to0\) would silently omit those arrays. The correction also prevents the existential constant in the theoretical plug-in rule from being presented as a numerical computation.

proposed_core_edits.proposed: \(\widehat L=L(\widehat{\mathbf P})\). The numerically explicit no-MOT rule \(B_N^{\mathrm{mean}}\) and the theoretically calibrated rule \(B_N^{\mathrm{plug}}\), for a finite \(C_d\) established to exist by the plug-in theorem, both belong to \(\mathcal H_\alpha\). The proved bounds are \(c_d\max\{N^{-1/2},K^{-2}(m\log m)^{-2/d}\}\le R_d(N,K)\le C_d[N^{-1/2}+\min\{r/K^2,K^{-1}m^{-2/d}\}]\) and \(c_{d,\alpha}N^{-1/2}\le E_{d,\alpha}(N,K)\le C_{d,\alpha}[N^{-1/2}+\min\{r/K^2,K^{-1}m^{-2/d}\}]\). Consequently both risks are of order \(N^{-1/2}\) when \(K\ge c_0N^{q_d}\); exact functions \(\rho_{\mathrm{est}}\) and \(\rho_{\mathrm{len}}\) remain unresolved on the residual small-ratio arrays.
proposed_core_edits.reason: The previous metadata advertised exact all-\(K\) equivalences through unresolved rate symbols. This post-image records only established estimating, confidence-bound, sandwich, and root-\(N\) results, distinguishes the explicit mean-floor procedure from the existentially calibrated plug-in rule, and leaves the residual frontier open.

proposed.comparator_claim: The published model permits all dimensions and \(K\ge2\). On the common fixed-\(d>4\), \(K\ge3\), balanced overlap, its arbitrary marginal class is the same \(\mathcal P(\mathbb B_d)^K\), and its balanced i.i.d. unit sampling induces the armwise product law used here; Theorem 1 gives \(N^{-1/2}+\min\{K^{-1},K^{-1/2}m^{-2/d}\}\).

proposed_core_edits.reason: The complete table now states the Gao--Ge--Qian common-class qualification, records the upward transfer of the published two-margin subclass converse, distinguishes the sharper \(q_d\) theoretical elbow from the independent mean-only no-MOT baseline, and removes any implication that the existentially calibrated plug-in lower bound is numerically reportable.

open_obligations.what_is_open: Determine matching all-estimator and ordered one-sided lower bounds, or a sharper matching computable upper procedure, on every subsequence with \(K_N/N^{q_d}\to0\), including exact fixed-\(K\) logarithms and every transition; then assemble these with the established root-\(N\) subsequences to cover every irregular legal array with \(\liminf_N K_N/N^{q_d}=0\).
open_obligations.obstruction: The available nonparametric converse is the embedded two-margin order \(K^{-2}(m\log m)^{-2/d}\), whereas the proved plug-in upper contribution is \(K^{-1}m^{-2/d}\). No instantiated simultaneous-marginal family currently preserves a separation of the missing order against every rematching column while keeping mixture total variation at most \(1/4\), and no sharper aggregate theorem for all jointly conjugate dual potentials is available. The theoretical plug-in confidence rule also contains an unspecified existence constant and therefore is not by itself a numerically calibrated solution.
open_obligations.attempted: The residual envelope, arbitrary-subset support exchange, optimal-sum diameter, common-support empirical interpolation, two-margin reduction, ordered Bernoulli pair, dimension-dependent root-\(N\) theorems, rational empirical-MOT certificate, sparse-arm gadgets, parity witnesses, and fixed-dimensional orthogonal constructions have been checked. The latter constructions do not close the arm factor because alternative margins can rematch, and neither the finite-family branch nor the aggregate-dual branch has supplied the missing certificate.
open_obligations.partial_result:
Under balanced armwise product sampling, unit-ball support, fixed \(d>4\), \(K\ge3\), and \(m=N/K\ge2\), the established finite-sample bounds are
\[
c_d\max\left\{N^{-1/2},K^{-2}(m\log m)^{-2/d}\right\}
\le R_d(N,K)
\le C_d\left[N^{-1/2}+\min\left\{\frac r{K^2},\frac1K m^{-2/d}\right\}\right]
\]
and
\[
c_{d,\alpha}N^{-1/2}
\le E_{d,\alpha}(N,K)
\le C_{d,\alpha}\left[N^{-1/2}+\min\left\{\frac r{K^2},\frac1K m^{-2/d}\right\}\right].
\]
Here \(r=\min\{K,d\}\), and the upper expected-length bound is attained by the theoretical rule \(B_N^{\mathrm{plug}}\) after choosing a finite constant \(C_d\) whose existence is proved by the plug-in upper theorem. This proves uniform root-\(N\) order for both risks whenever \(K\ge c_0N^{q_d}\), with
\[
q_5=\frac16,
\qquad
q_d=\frac14\quad\text{for }d\ge6.
\]
Independently, the mean-floor rule \(B_N^{\mathrm{mean}}\) is numerically explicit, requires no multi-marginal transport computation, is uniformly honest, and has worst-case expected excess length of order \(N^{-1/2}+r/K^2\); hence it yields a no-MOT root-\(N\) baseline when \(K\gtrsim N^{1/4}\). For rational empirical input, \(\mathsf{CertMOT}_\epsilon\) computes primal and dual certificates bracketing \(L(\widehat{\mathbf P})\) to any rational width \(\epsilon\), in fixed-dimensional time polynomial in \(N\) and \((K/\epsilon)^d\). What remains unresolved is a matching all-estimator and ordered one-sided converse, or a sharper matching upper bound, on every subsequence along which \(K_N/N^{q_d}\to0\), including fixed-\(K\) logarithms and all intervening transitions.

prose_updates.tldr: The target \(L(\mathbf P)\) is the sharp causal second moment compatible with the observed potential-outcome marginals, not a centered variance residual. On the common fixed-\(d>4\), \(K\ge3\), balanced arbitrary-margin class, the core sharpens Gao--Ge--Qian's empirical upper rate through the exact residual envelope and optimal-sum geometry. Matching root-\(N\) orders for minimax estimation and uniformly honest one-sided expected excess length are proved only when \(K\ge c_0N^{q_d}\), where \(q_5=1/6\) and \(q_d=1/4\) for \(d\ge6\); the exact smaller-arm frontier remains open, including irregular arrays with \(\liminf_NK_N/N^{q_d}=0\), fixed-\(K\) logarithms, and the ordered converse. The mean-floor lower bound is a separate numerically explicit no-MOT procedure and yields its own root-\(N\) baseline for \(K\gtrsim N^{1/4}\). The sharper plug-in lower bound is uniformly honest for a finite constant \(C_d\) proved to exist, but it is a theoretical calibration rather than a directly reportable numerical rule. The rational primal--dual procedure certifies the empirical MOT value to requested numerical width; it does not supply that statistical constant. The finite simultaneous-marginal template is defined but not instantiated. The STAR audit remains conditional on a known finite outcome bound, affine scaling, an i.i.d. superpopulation law, complete randomization, and randomized balanced subsampling, and does not validate the native \(161/37/36\) calculation.

project_justification.gap: On the common fixed-\(d>4\), \(K\ge3\), balanced class, Gao--Ge--Qian Theorem 1 has high-dimensional term \(K^{-1/2}m^{-2/d}\), while their Proposition 2 prints a two-margin lower expression with \((m\log m)^{-2/d}\) and supplies neither uniform one-sided coverage nor minimax expected excess length. Their published scope is broader in dimension and includes \(K=2\), but on this overlap both papers allow the same arbitrary laws in \(\mathcal P(\mathbb B_d)^K\), and their balanced i.i.d. setup induces this note's armwise product experiment. The embedded Manole--Niles-Weed lower bound is valid on a two-margin subclass and therefore transfers upward, but it does not settle the missing arm factor or fixed-\(K\) logarithm. The exact estimation and ordered one-sided frontiers remain unresolved precisely on subsequences where \(K_N/N^{q_d}\to0\), including those inside irregular arrays.
project_justification.niche: The squared-sum cost has shared fixed-dimensional geometry: all dual potentials obey one joint constraint, and optimal coupling atoms admit arbitrary-subset exchanges. A valid lower construction must nevertheless survive every alternative multi-arm rematching. The paper therefore separates three deliverables: a numerically explicit mean-only confidence floor, sharper theoretical plug-in rates, and a finite rational certificate handle for the unresolved simultaneous perturbation problem.
project_justification.fill: The project proves the sharp deterministic residual and support-diameter results, a tighter empirical plug-in upper bound, the dimension-dependent root-\(N\) elbow, matching root-\(N\) one-sided expected-length order in that region, an independently useful mean-floor no-MOT baseline, and a rational primal--dual bracket for the empirical endpoint. The theoretical plug-in confidence rule uses a finite \(C_d\) established to exist and is not called numerically explicit. The finite-support perturbation template is defined but not instantiated: endpoint separation, mixture indistinguishability, resistance to every rematching column with strict off-contact slack, and the ordered low-versus-high separation remain explicit targets. The residual question covers every legal array not eventually bounded below by a positive multiple of \(N^{q_d}\) through its small-ratio subsequences. The STAR audit separately declares the known bound, affine scale, superpopulation law, complete randomization, and balanced subsampling required for its conditional application statement.

prose_updates.related_work: Gao, Ge, and Qian define the same second-moment endpoint \(L(\mathbf P)\) and treat a published class covering all dimensions and \(K\ge2\). On the common fixed-\(d>4\), \(K\ge3\), balanced overlap, their distributional class is the same arbitrary \(\mathcal P(\mathbb B_d)^K\), and their balanced i.i.d. unit design induces the armwise product law used here. Their Theorem 1 gives the displayed empirical upper rate, while their high-dimensional minimax claim remains open. This core's sharper plug-in theorem and \(q_d\) elbow are comparisons only on that common class. Its mean-floor theorems are an independent, numerically explicit no-MOT route, not the sharp elbow. Manole and Niles-Weed provide the closest all-estimator lower architecture for quadratic two-margin transport. Because the two-margin construction is a subclass of the arbitrary-margin model, its lower bound transfers upward, but its \((m\log m)^{-2/d}\) order does not close the multi-arm gap. Binary covariate-aware transport results of Lin, Gao, Blanchet, and Glynn inform the causal framing but impose a different conditional structure and do not settle this unconditional growing-arm endpoint. Two-margin entropy transfer and Donsker results of Hundrieser and coauthors do not control an increasing jointly conjugate tuple. Work on vector mixability, selected scalar joint mixes, regular Monge stability, multiscale Wasserstein approximation, sliced-Wasserstein intervals, dual-feasible causal inference, and ordered moduli supplies neighboring geometry or inference tools but not the missing all-rematching simultaneous family or shared-dual aggregate bound. The finite-support MOT literature motivates the rational diagnostic but does not establish its required separation. The certified algorithm exploits the present fixed-dimensional squared-sum structure and is consistent with generic multimarginal hardness results. Gao--Ge--Qian's STAR application uses native cell sizes \(161,37,36\); the conditional audit here requires a known finite bound, affine rescaling, an i.i.d. superpopulation law, complete randomization, and randomized balanced subsampling and does not reproduce the native unequal-count tightening.
prose_updates.technical_internal_limitation: The unresolved class consists of every legal array with \(\liminf_NK_N/N^{q_d}=0\). A complete answer must work on every further subsequence where the ratio tends to zero and splice consistently with root-\(N\) subsequences, so oscillatory arrays cannot be removed by assuming a full-sequence limit. The known nonparametric lower term is \(K^{-2}(m\log m)^{-2/d}\), whereas the proved upper term may retain \(K^{-1}m^{-2/d}\). The finite-support perturbation template has not been instantiated with endpoint separation, mixture total variation at most \(1/4\), and positive reduced-cost slack off every declared contact set; tensoring two-margin, parity, or orthogonal gadgets fails because alternative arms may rematch. No sharper aggregate theorem for the jointly conjugate potentials is known. The plug-in confidence rule is uniformly honest only after choosing a finite theorem constant \(C_d\); absent its numerical value, the rule is theoretical rather than directly reportable. The mean-floor rule remains explicit and avoids MOT but has the coarser residual term \(r/K^2\). The certified computation theorem brackets only the empirical endpoint, is fixed-dimensional, and has polynomial dependence on \((K/\epsilon)^d\), not a generic exact-MOT guarantee. The STAR audit discards observations, depends on the declared known-bound superpopulation model, and does not reproduce the published native-cell computation.
prose_updates.honest_scope: The note fixes \(d>4\), assumes balanced armwise product sampling with \(K\ge3\) and \(m=N/K\to\infty\), allows arbitrary unit-ball marginals, and preserves the uncentered second-moment endpoint \(L\). The sharp residual envelope, support diameter, improved empirical upper bound, decision-risk sandwiches, dimension-dependent root-\(N\) frontier, theoretical plug-in honesty result, explicit mean-floor corollaries, numerical certificate, parity witness, and conditional STAR audit are established only under their displayed assumptions. Matching root-\(N\) estimation and one-sided expected-length orders are claimed only for \(K\ge c_0N^{q_d}\), with \(q_5=1/6\) and \(q_d=1/4\) for \(d\ge6\). The mean-only no-MOT route independently gives a coarser root-\(N\) baseline when \(K\gtrsim N^{1/4}\). The plug-in lower bound is a theoretical uniformly calibrated rule because its \(C_d\) is existential; only the mean-floor formula and the empirical MOT numerical bracket are directly computable from the stated information. No exact rate or ordered nonparametric length converse is claimed on small-ratio subsequences, and the simultaneous family is only a construction handle. The two-margin specialization is a definitional reduction and supplies a subclass converse, not a full multi-arm lower construction. The hypercube statement includes the legal \(K=3,d=5\) value \(1/9\). The STAR conclusion applies only after the declared scaling and randomized balanced subsampling and makes no claim for the native unequal cell counts.

proofs.proof_tex:
Fix \(d\ge 5\), \(K\ge 3\), and \(m\ge 2\), and let \(N=Km\) as required by Assumption~\texttt{ass:balanced-array}.  We first give a single data-driven upper-bound procedure that does not solve a multi-marginal transport problem.  Define
\[
 \widehat\mu_k=\frac1m\sum_{i=1}^m X_{ki},
 \qquad
 \bar X=\frac1K\sum_{k=1}^K\widehat\mu_k
       =\frac1N\sum_{k=1}^K\sum_{i=1}^m X_{ki},
 \qquad
 T_{\rm mean}=\|\bar X\|_2^2.
\]
This statistic is measurable and uses only the observations.  Under Assumption~\texttt{ass:product-experiment}, the centered vectors \(X_{ki}-\mu_k\) are mutually independent and have mean zero.  Consequently, using the inner-product expansion of a squared norm and the vanishing of every cross term,
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \mathbb E_{\mathbf P}\|\bar X-\bar\mu\|_2^2
 &=\frac1{N^2}\sum_{k=1}^K\sum_{i=1}^m
   \mathbb E_{\mathbf P}\|X_{ki}-\mu_k\|_2^2 \\
 &=\frac1{N^2}\sum_{k=1}^K\sum_{i=1}^m
   \left\{\mathbb E_{\mathbf P}\|X_{ki}\|_2^2-\|\mu_k\|_2^2\right\}
 \le \frac{Km}{N^2}=\frac1N.
 \end{aligned}                                                    \tag{1}
\]
The inequality uses \(X_{ki}\in\mathbb B_d\), which holds for every law in the model class appearing in Definition~\texttt{def:minimax-risk}.  Convexity of \(\mathbb B_d\) also gives \(\|\bar X\|_2\le1\) almost surely and \(\|\bar\mu\|_2\le1\).  Therefore the difference-of-squares identity, Cauchy--Schwarz, and then Jensen's inequality applied to (1) yield
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \mathbb E_{\mathbf P}
   \left|T_{\rm mean}-\|\bar\mu\|_2^2\right|
 &\le \mathbb E_{\mathbf P}
   \left[(\|\bar X\|_2+\|\bar\mu\|_2)
          \|\bar X-\bar\mu\|_2\right] \\
 &\le 2\left(\mathbb E_{\mathbf P}
                  \|\bar X-\bar\mu\|_2^2\right)^{1/2}
 \le 2N^{-1/2}.                                      \tag{2}
 \end{aligned}
\]

The deterministic geometry in Theorem~\texttt{thm:sharp-residual-envelope}, together with the definition \(V(\mathbf P)=K^2\{L(\mathbf P)-\|\bar\mu\|_2^2\}\), gives
\[
 0\le L(\mathbf P)-\|\bar\mu\|_2^2\le \frac r{K^2}.             \tag{3}
\]
Division is legitimate because \(K\ge3\).  Combining (2) and (3) by the triangle inequality gives, uniformly over \(\mathbf P\in\mathcal P(\mathbb B_d)^K\),
\[
 \mathbb E_{\mathbf P}|T_{\rm mean}-L(\mathbf P)|
 \le 2N^{-1/2}+\frac r{K^2}
 \le 2\left(N^{-1/2}+\frac r{K^2}\right).             \tag{4}
\]
Taking the supremum over \(\mathbf P\) and then using \(T_{\rm mean}\) as a competitor in the infimum in Definition~\texttt{def:minimax-risk} proves the claimed upper bound with \(C_d=2\).  This is a deterministic-bias plus second-moment argument; in particular, its estimator is the mean-only statistic above.

For the all-estimator lower bound, use the two distributions supplied by Lemma~\texttt{lem:bernoulli-two-point}.  Write \(Q_j=\bigotimes_{k=1}^K(P_k^{(j)})^{\otimes m}\), \(L_j=L(\mathbf P^{(j)})\), and \(\Delta=L_1-L_0\).  The lemma gives
\[
 \Delta\ge aN^{-1/2}>0,
 \qquad
 \operatorname{TV}(Q_0,Q_1)\le\frac14.                         \tag{5}
\]
For an arbitrary measurable estimator \(T\), define the test
\(\phi=\mathbf 1\{T\ge(L_0+L_1)/2\}\).  On \(\{\phi=1\}\) under \(Q_0\), one has \(|T-L_0|\ge\Delta/2\), while on \(\{\phi=0\}\) under \(Q_1\), one has \(|T-L_1|\ge\Delta/2\).  Hence
\[
 \mathbb E_{Q_0}|T-L_0|+\mathbb E_{Q_1}|T-L_1|
 \ge \frac\Delta2\{Q_0(\phi=1)+Q_1(\phi=0)\}.                  \tag{6}
\]
For the event \(A=\{\phi=1\}\), the definition of total variation gives directly
\[
 Q_0(A)+Q_1(A^c)
 =1-\{Q_1(A)-Q_0(A)\}
 \ge1-\operatorname{TV}(Q_0,Q_1)
 \ge\frac34.                                                     \tag{7}
\]
Equations (5)--(7) imply
\[
 \max_{j\in\{0,1\}}\mathbb E_{Q_j}|T-L_j|
 \ge \frac{3\Delta}{16}
 \ge \frac{3a}{16}N^{-1/2}.                                    \tag{8}
\]
Both \(\mathbf P^{(0)}\) and \(\mathbf P^{(1)}\) belong to the supremum in Definition~\texttt{def:minimax-risk}; taking the infimum of (8) over every measurable \(T\) therefore proves the lower bound.  Thus one may take
\[
 c_d=\min\left\{\frac{3a}{16},2\right\},
 \qquad C_d=2,
\]
which ensures \(0<c_d\le C_d<\infty\).

Finally choose \(c_0=1\).  If \(K\ge c_0N^{1/4}\), then \(r=\min\{K,d\}\le d\) and
\[
 \frac r{K^2}\le\frac d{K^2}\le dN^{-1/2}.                    \tag{9}
\]
Substitution of (9) into (4), together with (8), gives
\[
 c_dN^{-1/2}\le R_d(N,K)\le 2(1+d)N^{-1/2}.
\]
The constants are independent of \(N\), \(K\), \(m\), and \(\mathbf P\).  Assumption~\texttt{ass:legal-triangular-array} restricts the asymptotic assertion to balanced sequences with \(m_N=N/K_N\to\infty\); because all preceding inequalities are finite-sample and uniform, they apply term by term along every such sequence.  This establishes the stated sufficient root-\(N\) region as a mean-only, no-transport baseline; it makes no assertion that \(N^{1/4}\) is the sharp elbow.

Put
\[
\varepsilon_N=(\alpha N)^{-1/2}.
\]
Fix an arbitrary
\(\mathbf P=(P_1,\ldots,P_K)\in\mathcal P(\mathbb B_d)^K\).
By Assumption~\texttt{ass:balanced-array},
\(N=Km\), and hence, using the arm means in the frozen core,
\[
\mathbb E_{\mathbf P}\bar X
=\frac{1}{N}\sum_{k=1}^K\sum_{i=1}^m\mu_k
=\frac{m}{N}\sum_{k=1}^K\mu_k
=\bar\mu.
\tag{1}
\]
Assumption~\texttt{ass:product-experiment} makes all centered summands
\(X_{ki}-\mu_k\) independent, so their cross inner products have mean
zero.  Since each \(P_k\) is a probability measure on \(\mathbb B_d\),
\[
\mathbb E_{P_k}\|X_{ki}-\mu_k\|_2^2
=\mathbb E_{P_k}\|X_{ki}\|_2^2-\|\mu_k\|_2^2
\le 1.
\]
It follows from (1) that
\[
\mathbb E_{\mathbf P}\|\bar X-\bar\mu\|_2^2
=\frac{1}{N^2}\sum_{k=1}^K\sum_{i=1}^m
  \mathbb E_{P_k}\|X_{ki}-\mu_k\|_2^2
\le \frac{1}{N}.
\tag{2}
\]
The pointwise inequality
\[
\mathbf 1\{\|\bar X-\bar\mu\|_2>\varepsilon_N\}
\le
\frac{\|\bar X-\bar\mu\|_2^2}{\varepsilon_N^2}
\]
and (2) therefore give
\[
\Pr_{\mathbf P}\{\|\bar X-\bar\mu\|_2\le\varepsilon_N\}
\ge 1-\alpha.
\tag{3}
\]
No asymptotic approximation is used in this step.

On the event in (3), the reverse triangle inequality yields
\[
\max\{0,\|\bar X\|_2-\varepsilon_N\}\le\|\bar\mu\|_2.
\]
Theorem~\texttt{thm:sharp-residual-envelope} gives
\(L(\mathbf P)-\|\bar\mu\|_2^2=V(\mathbf P)/K^2\ge0\).
Consequently Definition~\texttt{def:mean-lower-bound} implies
\[
B_N^{\mathrm{mean}}
=\bigl(\max\{0,\|\bar X\|_2-\varepsilon_N\}\bigr)^2
\le \|\bar\mu\|_2^2
\le L(\mathbf P)
\]
on an event of probability at least \(1-\alpha\), uniformly over
\(\mathbf P\).  Definition~\texttt{def:honest-bounds} thus proves
\[
B_N^{\mathrm{mean}}\in\mathcal H_\alpha.
\tag{4}
\]

We next bound the expected excess length of this particular honest
rule.  Set \(q=\|\bar\mu\|_2\) and \(t=\|\bar X\|_2\).  Convexity of
\(\mathbb B_d\) gives \(q,t\in[0,1]\).  Theorem
\texttt{thm:sharp-residual-envelope} gives
\[
0\le L(\mathbf P)-q^2\le\frac r{K^2}.
\tag{5}
\]
For every \(t\in[0,1]\) and every \(\varepsilon>0\),
\[
0\le t^2-(t-\varepsilon)_+^2\le2\varepsilon.
\tag{6}
\]
Indeed, if \(t\ge\varepsilon\), the middle expression is
\(2t\varepsilon-\varepsilon^2\le2\varepsilon\); if
\(t<\varepsilon\), it is \(t^2\le t\varepsilon\le\varepsilon\).
Also,
\[
|q^2-t^2|=(q+t)|q-t|
\le2\|\bar X-\bar\mu\|_2,
\tag{7}
\]
where the last inequality uses the reverse triangle inequality.
Combining (5)--(7) with
\((a+b)_+\le a+|b|\) for \(a\ge0\), and then applying the
Cauchy--Schwarz inequality and (2), gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
\mathbb E_{\mathbf P}
 \bigl[(L(\mathbf P)-B_N^{\mathrm{mean}})_+\bigr]
&\le
\frac r{K^2}
+\mathbb E_{\mathbf P}|q^2-t^2|
+\mathbb E_{\mathbf P}\{t^2-(t-\varepsilon_N)_+^2\}\\
&\le
\frac r{K^2}
+2\mathbb E_{\mathbf P}\|\bar X-\bar\mu\|_2
+2\varepsilon_N\\
&\le
\frac r{K^2}
+2N^{-1/2}
+2\alpha^{-1/2}N^{-1/2}.
\end{aligned}
\tag{8}
\]
Taking the supremum over \(\mathbf P\) in (8), then using (4) as a
feasible rule in Definition~\texttt{def:minimax-excess-length}, proves
\[
E_{d,\alpha}(N,K)
\le C_{d,\alpha}\left(N^{-1/2}+\frac r{K^2}\right)
\tag{9}
\]
for a finite positive constant \(C_{d,\alpha}\) depending only on
\(d\) and \(\alpha\).

For the matching all-procedure lower bound, invoke
Lemma~\texttt{lem:bernoulli-two-point}.  Write
\(L_j=L(\mathbf P^{(j)})\), let
\(\Delta=L_1-L_0\ge aN^{-1/2}\), and denote the corresponding product
experiment laws by \(\mathbb Q_0,\mathbb Q_1\).  They satisfy
\(\operatorname{TV}(\mathbb Q_0,\mathbb Q_1)\le1/4\).
For an arbitrary \(B_N\in\mathcal H_\alpha\), honesty at the lower
endpoint law and the defining total-variation inequality imply
\[
\mathbb Q_1(B_N\le L_0)
\ge\mathbb Q_0(B_N\le L_0)
  -\operatorname{TV}(\mathbb Q_0,\mathbb Q_1)
\ge1-\alpha-\frac14
>\frac12,
\tag{10}
\]
where the last strict inequality uses \(\alpha\in(0,1/4)\).  On
\(\{B_N\le L_0\}\), one has
\((L_1-B_N)_+\ge L_1-L_0=\Delta\).  Therefore
\[
\sup_{\mathbf P}
\mathbb E_{\mathbf P}\bigl[(L(\mathbf P)-B_N)_+\bigr]
\ge
\mathbb E_{\mathbb Q_1}[(L_1-B_N)_+]
\ge\frac{\Delta}{2}
\ge\frac a2N^{-1/2}.
\tag{11}
\]
Because (11) holds for every honest \(B_N\), taking the infimum in
Definition~\texttt{def:minimax-excess-length} proves the lower bound
with \(c_{d,\alpha}=a/2>0\).

Finally, if \(K\ge c_0N^{1/4}\), then \(r=\min\{K,d\}\le d\) and
\[
\frac r{K^2}\le\frac{d}{c_0^2}N^{-1/2}.
\tag{12}
\]
Equations (9), (11), and (12) yield
\(E_{d,\alpha}(N,K)\asymp N^{-1/2}\).  Assumption
\texttt{ass:legal-triangular-array} restricts the admissible
asymptotic sequences through \(m_N=N/K_N\to\infty\); all inequalities
above are finite-sample statements at each admissible index, so this
restriction requires no further limiting step.
